title: Jimbocho kissaten crawl
when: Any weekday morning; most are shut Sundays
why: Seven of the national top-100 kissaten inside a few blocks. Pick three, not seven.

title: Ginkgo morning, Aoyama day
why: Leaves before the crowds, then the best coffee and tea concentration in Tokyo, all on foot.

title: Yanesen on foot
why: Old wooden Tokyo, a lacquered shrine, and a kissaten that opens early enough to beat the queue.

title: Knives and Kuramae
why: Kappabashi in its quiet window, top-100 ramen or tonkatsu for lunch, done by mid-afternoon.

title: Ginza into the night
why: Aged coffee, the food hall before close, two illuminations, then a proper bar.

title: Home-turf morning
why: Shrine, Confucian temple, top-100 kissaten, then soba — all inside a 15-minute radius of the hotel.
